newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Somincor says production partially resumed.
newsitem.headline: Somincor says production partially resumed.

text.p: Portuguese state owned company Somincor said Thursday that production had partially resumed at the Neves Corvo copper mine where miners have been on strike since Monday.
"The mine is working at 80 percent capacity," said Maria de Fatima Nunes, a spokswomen for Somincor.
The spokswoman said workers who did not support the strike took advantage of the absense of pickets of striking miners to enter the mine and start work.
Busloads of strikers had abandoned picket lines to travel the 250 kms to Lisbon to lobby the Somincor headquarters and the Economy Ministry.
The miners took the protest to Lisbon after talks with mine management on the dispute over working hours had failed, earlier on Thursday.
Unions reject company plans to impose Sunday shift working.
The spokswoman said that 75 workers, a little over 50 percent of the usual shift, had turned up for work.
She reafirmed that the company is ready to negotiate but would not drop its insistence on Sunday working.
The Neves Corvo copper mine, Europe's largest, produced 107,00 tonnes of copper in 1996.
